name: Drone delivery (US)
title: Drone delivery in the US: waiting on FAA Part 108
question: Is drone delivery about to become viable in the US?
answer: US drone delivery has been capped by waivers: each operator needs FAA exemptions to fly beyond the pilot's line of sight. The FAA proposed Part 108 to make those flights routine in August 2025 (RIN 2120-AL82), and a June 2025 executive order told it to finish quickly. As of 25 October 2026 no final rule has been published, so the trigger is pending.
verdict_reason: The enabling rule is proposed but not final. The board resolves its call automatically from the Federal Register.

constraint.name: Routine beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight
constraint.detail: Without a standing rule, every delivery network needs case-by-case exemptions, which caps scale.

crossing.text: Final rule for 14 CFR part 108 (RIN 2120-AL82) not yet published.

graveyard_note: Not enumerated yet. Before calling this category ripe, the board needs named, funded drone-delivery companies that died on the waiver regime, with sources.
